analysis: Examined desktop-app/package-lock.json (base-side excerpts at lines 5478-7022, plus the patch excerpt and changed ranges). The change is a dependency bump: electron 44.5.1 -> 44.9.1, vite 8.3.2 -> 8.3.5, and rolldown 1.2.12 -> 1.2.15 with its @rolldown/binding-* optional packages. It also moves @oxc-project/types 0.152.0 -> 0.155.0, and the postcss/picomatch/undici ranges shift slightly. All entries I could see resolve from registry.npmjs.org and carry sha512 integrity hashes, so I saw no lockfile tampering such as a non-registry resolved URL, a dropped integrity field, or a new git/file dependency. The excerpt I saw covers only base text and a truncated patch; the head-side lock entries beyond the patch excerpt (for example the electron and vite resolved URLs and hashes) were not visible. I therefore cannot verify the new integrity values, and I recorded that as a coverage limit rather than a finding. The desktop app is a console/GUI wrapper, outside the provider/native-runtime scope of this threat model. It does not touch TB-002, TB-011, A-003 or the attestation paths, so I identified no change to the provider attestation, E2E encryption, App Attest or fan-helper security behavior. Remaining question: confirm that the Electron 44.9.1 bump has no packaging or code-signing side effects on the shipped desktop app. That falls under the build/release pipeline, not the supplied evidence. No findings.
